title: Quantum Computing Case Study for Telecom | NTT DOCOMO
summary: Japan’s largest mobile operator reduced peak location-registration and paging signals with its second D-Wave-powered quantum application in production.

## Article Highlights


### Japan’s largest mobile operator reduced peak location-registration signals by 65.3% and peak paging signals by 7% across a 333 base station segment, improving network efficiency with its second D-Wave-powered production application.


**THE CHALLENGE**


NTT DOCOMO needed to reduce paging and location-registration signals across a national network of roughly 250,000 base stations. The goal was to lower signaling load while maintaining network performance and connectivity, a computationally complex optimization problem that was challenging and impractical to solve using the customer’s existing classical solutions.


**THE D-WAVE SOLUTION**


Building on its first successful production application, NTT DOCOMO expanded its use of D-Wave™ technology to address a broader and more complex network optimization problem. The second hybrid-quantum application minimizes paging and location-registration signals simultaneously using D-Wave’s quantum technology.


**THE RESULT**


After optimizing a segment with 333 base stations, NTT DOCOMO realized:


- 65.3% reduction in peak location-registration signals


- 7% reduction in peak paging signals


- Approximately five-minute time-to-solution for a problem that the customer’s classical-only approaches could not solve within a production-relevant timeline.


**The application has since been deployed and is now in operation nationwide.**


## **Japan's Largest Mobile Carrier Faces a Growing Signaling Challenge**


NTT DOCOMO (DOCOMO), Japan's largest mobile operator, serves more than 93 million subscriptions across a national network of roughly 250,000 base stations. Every phone, smartwatch, and connected device relies on two types of background signals to remain reachable. Devices send location-registration signals to update the network as they move into new areas, while the network sends paging signals to locate a device when a call or message arrives.


Like many telecommunications operators, DOCOMO manages these signals by dividing its network into tracking areas (TAs), which are grouped into larger tracking-area lists (TA-Lists). The network sends paging signals within individual TAs, while a device sends a location-registration signal when it moves from one TA-List to another.


Reducing both signal types is a longstanding challenge for DOCOMO and the broader telecommunications industry because changes that lower one can increase the other. Smaller TA-Lists trigger more frequent location-registration signals, while larger TA-Lists require paging signals to be sent across more base stations when a call or message arrives.


At DOCOMO's scale, the underlying optimization problem is enormous. For example, a network segment with 333 base stations grouped into three TA-Lists and nine TAs has 2


8991


possible configurations, vastly more than the number of atoms in the universe. The model must also account for operational constraints, such as avoiding registration boundaries along high-traffic areas like rail lines and highways. Multiplied across DOCOMO's full national footprint, the search space is far beyond what classical solvers can address on a production-relevant timeline.


"With our second production application powered by D-Wave's hybrid quantum technology, we are applying quantum optimization to a broader and more complex area of network operations."


— Hiroshi Kawakami, Senior Manager, Data Platform Department, NTT DOCOMO, INC.


## **Building on Quantum Success in Production**


DOCOMO had already demonstrated the value of quantum optimization in its network. Since 2024, the carrier has been using D-Wave's constrained quadratic model (CQM) hybrid solver in a production application to optimize paging-signal traffic within individual TAs. Using mobile traffic data from three regions, the application reorganized 270 base stations into 21 TA-Lists. The problem took DOCOMO’s classical computing methods 27 hours to solve, compared with just 40 seconds using D-Wave’s platform. Once deployed in production, the application reduced peak-period paging signals by roughly 15%, giving DOCOMO’s network an estimated 20% more capacity for connected devices.


That result gave DOCOMO the technical foundation to apply quantum computing to a harder problem: optimizing across TA-Lists and TAs together to reduce paging and location-registration signals simultaneously.


"DOCOMO is showing telecom operators around the world what production quantum adoption looks like: move beyond a single use case and apply the technology to distinct, increasingly complex operational challenges."


— Dr. Alan Baratz, CEO, D-Wave


## **Optimizing Two Competing Signals at Once**


DOCOMO aggregated real device-movement data between base stations across its network and formulated a multi-objective optimization problem. The application reassigns base stations to TA-Lists and TAs to minimize both paging and location-registration signals, balancing the trade-off between the two. It also avoids placing registration boundaries along major transit routes, where fast-moving devices would otherwise trigger bursts of unnecessary signaling, increasing the burden on base stations.


"The application balances two competing network requirements, significantly reducing location-registration signaling while also lowering paging signals. Together with our first production application, it demonstrates how quantum computing can help us address multiple aspects of network optimization and use our infrastructure more efficiently. "


— Hiroshi Kawakami, Senior Manager, Data Platform Department, NTT DOCOMO, INC.


## **From a Five-Minute Solve to a Production Application**


DOCOMO addressed the problem using D-Wave's CQM hybrid solver, which combines classical computing with the Advantage2™ annealing quantum computer, through the


[Leap™ quantum cloud service](https://www.dwavequantum.com/solutions-and-products/cloud-platform/) . For a segment of 333 base stations, three TA-Lists, and nine TAs, the solver completed the optimization in approximately five minutes. DOCOMO’s previous classical methods could not solve this problem within the time required for production use.


DOCOMO also built a map-based visualization tool that converts the application’s output into a base-station reassignment plan. Regional branch offices can review the plan and estimated signal reductions before approving deployment. The application has now been rolled out across DOCOMO’s live national network.


The graph shows the reduction of location-registration signals after the implementation of the quantum network optimization application.


Across the 333 base station segment, the application reduced the daily peak volume of location-registration signals by 65.3% and paging signals by 7%, solving a challenge engineers previously thought impossible to address. Together, the reductions lower the network’s control-plane load and free up capacity to support continued growth in connected devices.


"Telecom networks are highly complex, resource-constrained environments, and these results demonstrate how D-Wave's annealing quantum computing technology can help operators improve network performance and efficiency today."


— Dr. Alan Baratz, CEO, D-Wave
